title: A 3x3.3mm Configurable Gamma Photon Spectrometer for Precision Radioguided Cancer Resection
problem: Radioguided surgery (RGS) for cancer removal requires gamma-sensing probes that can detect lesions at depth, differentiate lesion size/depth, and operate with high specificity; existing probes lack configurability, form-factor, and energy resolution.
motivation: Microscopic cancer cell clusters are difficult to visualize intraoperatively; gamma-ray sensing enables detection at tissue depth with better localization than visible light, but current probes lack the resolution and configurability needed for differentiation.
method: A 180nm CMOS gamma spectrometer ASIC provides: (1) mm-scale pixelated design with single-gamma sensitivity, (2) per-pixel configurability for adaptive gain/threshold based on flux and PVT, (3) energy-resolving scheme with dynamic range to encode lesion depth via gamma energy profiles.
key_novelty: Configurable pixel-level gamma detection with energy-resolving capability to encode lesion depth/size differentiation in radioguided surgery.
contributions: Per-pixel configurability for flux and PVT adaptation
Depth encoding via gamma energy scattering profiles
limitations: Abstract-only; detection efficiency, energy resolution (keV), position resolution, acquisition time, and in-vivo clinical validation not discussed.
primary_theme: Configurable pixelated gamma spectrometer for intraoperative cancer detection
